title: Console onboarding nudge component: UX + CTA copy + dismissal behavior + accessibility
creator: Tessa Morgan
body:
## Context
We’re shipping a reusable **OnboardingNudge** component for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint (Hosted API). This ticket covers the UX details that directly affect activation: info density, CTA labeling, dismissal/snooze behavior, and accessibility requirements.

The product/targeting framework and metrics are defined in Confluence (Console Onboarding Nudges – Experiment Framework). This design task converts that into buildable UI + copy specs and resolves edge cases we saw in early QA.

## Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-success by making the “next best action” obvious in <10 seconds of scanning.
- Keep nudges **non-blocking** and respectful (easy to dismiss; persistent rules prevent spam).
- Make CTA copy consistent across Console and lifecycle emails (per Soojin’s guidelines).
- Ensure component meets accessibility expectations (WCAG AA contrast, keyboard, SR labels).

## Non-goals
- Reworking Console IA, adding new onboarding pages, or writing full quickstart docs.
- Adding more than 1 primary nudge per surface (that’s a PM/experiment decision).

---

## Decision summary (what we’re shipping)
### 1) Info density / layout
**Chosen pattern:** compact, dismissible card (no modal).
- Title (1 line, max 48 chars; wraps to 2 lines if needed)
- Body (1 line preferred; max 2 lines; no more than ~140 chars)
- One primary CTA button
- Optional secondary text link (“Learn more”) only when the primary CTA is in-console (e.g., code drawer).
- Controls on the right: “Not now” (text button) + overflow (kebab) for permanent dismissal.

**Rationale:** In early dogfood, dense multi-bullet cards were skipped. The compact card kept attention on the action and avoided looking like marketing content.

**Visual notes:**
- Use a subtle accent border + icon only if it doesn’t increase height beyond ~96px in default state.
- Keep the CTA aligned baseline with title/body block (avoid “button floating” when body wraps).

### 2) CTA labeling standards
Rule: CTA labels must be explicit verbs + object (no “Get started”, no “Click here”).

**Approved CTAs (v1):**
- API key step (S1): **“Create API key”**
- First request step (S2), variants for experiment flag:
  - Variant A: **“Copy quickstart snippet”** (opens code drawer)
  - Variant B: **“Open quickstart”** (docs, new tab)
  - Variant C: **“Try in Playground”** (prefilled)
- Streaming accelerator (S3): **“Enable streaming example”** (code drawer)
- Usage value step (S3+): **“View usage”** (routes to dashboard)

**CTA microcopy (secondary helper text, optional, not a second CTA):**
- Allowed: “Opens in new tab”, “Copies to clipboard”, “Prefills Playground” (as subtle hint text under CTA *only* when ambiguous).

### 3) Dismissal behavior (snooze vs permanent)
We need two different user intents:
- “Not now” = temporary (snooze)
- “Don’t show again” = permanent

**Spec:**
- Primary dismiss action is **“Not now”** (text button). On click:
  - Hide immediately
  - Snooze for **72 hours** (per framework)
  - Track event: console_onboarding_nudge_dismissed (dismiss_type=snooze)
- Overflow menu includes:
  - “Don’t show again” (permanent)
  - “Why am I seeing this?” (optional, if we can ship help content; otherwise omit)
  - Track event with dismiss_type=permanent

**Persistence UX rules:**
- Dismiss controls must not move layout on hover/focus (no shifting).
- Do not re-render the same nudge more than **3 sessions** if state hasn’t changed (handled by targeting logic, but design calls this out as a requirement).

**Edge case:** if user dismisses “Create API key” but navigates to API Keys page directly, we still allow contextual helper content on that page (no blocking), but we do NOT re-show the global nudge card within the snooze window.

### 4) Accessibility requirements (must-have)
- Keyboard:
  - Tab order: Title/body (not focusable) → Primary CTA → “Not now” → overflow menu.
  - Overflow menu must be fully keyboard navigable and esc-closes.
- Screen reader:
  - Component has an accessible label (e.g., “Onboarding tip”).
  - Dismiss actions must have explicit aria-labels: “Snooze onboarding tip” / “Dismiss onboarding tip permanently”.
- Contrast:
  - All text and buttons meet WCAG AA (especially text-button “Not now”).
- Motion:
  - Any entrance animation must respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- Target size:
  - Click targets for dismiss controls ≥ 32px.

---

## Copy spec (v1)
All copy aligns to Messaging Guidelines (developer-first, concrete, no unverified claims).

### N1 — API key
Title: **Create an API key to send your first request**
Body: **Keys authenticate requests from your app or local dev.**
CTA: **Create API key**

### N2 — First request (variant-dependent CTA)
Title: **Run a minimal request (copy/paste)**
Body: **Validate your setup with the smallest working example.**
CTA (variant A/B/C): see CTA standards above

### N3 — Streaming
Title: **See tokens sooner with streaming**
Body: **Streaming reduces perceived latency and speeds up iteration.**
CTA: **Enable streaming example**

### N4 — Usage
Title: **Track usage + latency for your first calls**
Body: **See token usage, request latency, and errors in one place.**
CTA: **View usage**

Notes:
- Avoid “enterprise-grade” as lead message in these nudges.
- Avoid any numeric latency/cost claims.

---

## Component states
- Default (eligible): compact card
- Hover/focus: show controls without layout shift
- Dismissed (snooze): removed from DOM (no placeholder)
- Dismissed (permanent): removed until state changes
- Loading/unknown onboarding state: do not render nudge (avoid flicker)

---

## Deliverables
- Figma: Redwood Console → Growth Experiments → Onboarding Nudges (component + placements)
  - File: `Console / Onboarding Nudges (LGX)`
  - Page: `OnboardingNudge component spec (v1)`
  - Components:
    - OnboardingNudge/Card
    - Overflow menu (dismiss)
    - Code drawer entry point (visual only)
- Copy doc block added to Figma + shared with Marissa + Ben for review.

---

## QA notes (design sign-off checklist)
- [x] CTA labels are explicit and match actions.
- [x] “Not now” is visible and doesn’t look like a destructive action.
- [x] Overflow menu doesn’t steal focus; esc closes.
- [x] Text wraps gracefully at narrow widths (mobile / small laptop).
- [x] Contrast passes AA on both light + dark themes.
- [x] No nudges are positioned in a way that blocks API key creation modal or Playground send button.

---

## Open questions (resolved in this ticket)
1) Primary dismiss label: chose “Not now” over “Dismiss” (tested as less negative / clearer temporary intent).
2) Secondary CTA: allowed only when it’s truly secondary (e.g., “Learn more” to docs). Default is single CTA.
3) Should we show a checklist instead of a single card? Not in scope; framework says 1 at a time.

---
